title: Rigveda 8.36: To Indra
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 8.36: To Indra: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 8.36 is a hymn of 7 verses addressed to Indra. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 8, the book of the Kaṇva and Aṅgiras poets. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 609v-610r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 8.36.1-5 (aṣṭaka 6, adhyāya 3, varga 18); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 609v
translation.original_text:
1a̱vi̱tāsi̍ sunva̱to vṛ̱ktaba̍rhiṣa̱ḥ pibā̱ soma̱m madā̍ya̱ kaṁ śa̍takrato | yaṁ te̍ bhā̱gam adhā̍raya̱n viśvā̍ḥ sehā̱naḥ pṛta̍nā u̱ru jraya̱ḥ sam a̍psu̱jin ma̱rutvā̍m̐ indra satpate ||
2prāva̍ sto̱tāra̍m maghava̱nn ava̱ tvām pibā̱ soma̱m madā̍ya̱ kaṁ śa̍takrato | yaṁ te̍ bhā̱gam adhā̍raya̱n viśvā̍ḥ sehā̱naḥ pṛta̍nā u̱ru jraya̱ḥ sam a̍psu̱jin ma̱rutvā̍m̐ indra satpate ||
3ū̱rjā de̱vām̐ ava̱sy oja̍sā̱ tvām pibā̱ soma̱m madā̍ya̱ kaṁ śa̍takrato | yaṁ te̍ bhā̱gam adhā̍raya̱n viśvā̍ḥ sehā̱naḥ pṛta̍nā u̱ru jraya̱ḥ sam a̍psu̱jin ma̱rutvā̍m̐ indra satpate ||
4ja̱ni̱tā di̱vo ja̍ni̱tā pṛ̍thi̱vyāḥ pibā̱ soma̱m madā̍ya̱ kaṁ śa̍takrato | yaṁ te̍ bhā̱gam adhā̍raya̱n viśvā̍ḥ sehā̱naḥ pṛta̍nā u̱ru jraya̱ḥ sam a̍psu̱jin ma̱rutvā̍m̐ indra satpate ||
5ja̱ni̱tāśvā̍nāṁ jani̱tā gavā̍m asi̱ pibā̱ soma̱m madā̍ya̱ kaṁ śa̍takrato | yaṁ te̍ bhā̱gam adhā̍raya̱n viśvā̍ḥ sehā̱naḥ pṛta̍nā u̱ru jraya̱ḥ sam a̍psu̱jin ma̱rutvā̍m̐ indra satpate ||
translation.text:
1THOU helpest him whose grass is trimmed, who sheds the juice, O Ṣatakratu, drink Soma to make thee glad. The share which they have fixed for thee, thou, Indra, Victor o'er all hosts and space, begirt with Maruts, Lord of Heroes, winner of the floods.
2Maghavan, help thy worshipper: let him help thee. O Ṣatakratu, drink Soma to make thee glad. The share which they have fixed for thee, etc.
3Thou aidest Gods with food, and that with might aids thee, O Ṣatakratu, drink Soma to make thee glad.
4Creator of the heaven, creator of the earth, O Ṣatakratu, drink Soma to make thee glad.
5Father of cattle, father of all steeds art thou. O Ṣatakratu, drink Soma to make thee glad.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 609v (numbered 31v by the scribe) (OPenn image 610, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 8.35.16 ‹rakṣāṃsi sedhatam amīvāḥ sa-joṣasau›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 610r (numbered 32r by the scribe), begins in RV 8.36.6 ‹-indra sat-pate›. Verses 8.36.1-5 end on this page.

translation.original_ref: RV 8.36.6-7 (aṣṭaka 6, adhyāya 3, varga 18); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 610r
translation.original_text:
6atrī̍ṇā̱ṁ stoma̍m adrivo ma̱has kṛ̍dhi̱ pibā̱ soma̱m madā̍ya̱ kaṁ śa̍takrato | yaṁ te̍ bhā̱gam adhā̍raya̱n viśvā̍ḥ sehā̱naḥ pṛta̍nā u̱ru jraya̱ḥ sam a̍psu̱jin ma̱rutvā̍m̐ indra satpate ||
7śyā̱vāśva̍sya sunva̱tas tathā̍ śṛṇu̱ yathāśṛ̍ṇo̱r atre̱ḥ karmā̍ṇi kṛṇva̱taḥ | pra tra̱sada̍syum āvitha̱ tvam eka̱ in nṛ̱ṣāhya̱ indra̱ brahmā̍ṇi va̱rdhaya̍n ||
translation.text:
6Stone-hurler, glorify the Atris' hymn of praise. O Ṣatakratu, drink Soma to make thee glad.
7Hear thou Ṣyâvâṣva while he pours to thee, as erst thou heardest Atri when he wrought his holy rites. Indra, thou only gavest Trasadasyu aid in the fierce fight with heroes, strengthening his prayers.
